text: Under the 1987 Constitution, a Senator must be at least how many years old on the day of the election?
explanation: Art. VI, Sec. 3 requires a Senator to be a natural-born citizen, at least 35 years old on the day of the election, able to read and write, a registered voter, and a resident of the Philippines for at least two years immediately before the election.
hint: It is higher than the age for a district representative but lower than the age for the President.
whyA: 25 is the minimum age for a member of the House of Representatives (Art. VI, Sec. 6), not a Senator.
whyB: 30 is not an age requirement for any member of Congress under Art. VI.
whyD: 40 is the minimum age for the President and Vice-President (Art. VII, Secs. 2 and 3).
explanationTl: Sa Art. VI, Sec. 3, ang Senator ay dapat natural-born citizen, at least 35 years old sa mismong araw ng election, marunong magbasa at magsulat, registered voter, at resident ng Pilipinas nang at least two years bago ang election.
hintTl: Mas mataas ito sa age ng congressman, pero mas mababa sa age ng President.

text: Under the 1987 Constitution, the President is elected for a term of six years. Which rule on reelection applies to the President?
optionA: The President may be reelected for one more consecutive term.
optionB: The President is not eligible for any reelection.
optionC: The President may be reelected once if Congress approves by a two-thirds vote.
optionD: The President may be reelected as long as total service does not exceed ten years.
explanation: Art. VII, Sec. 4 states that the President shall not be eligible for any reelection. The six-year term is a single term.
hint: Think of the six-year term as a one-time term.
whyA: Art. VII, Sec. 4 bars any reelection, so there is no second consecutive term.
whyC: Congress has no power to allow a presidential reelection; the bar is in the Constitution itself.
whyD: There is no ten-year cap rule; the Constitution simply bars reelection.
explanationTl: Sa Art. VII, Sec. 4, malinaw na ang President ay hindi na pwedeng ma-reelect kahit kailan. Isang six-year term lang talaga.
hintTl: Isipin mo na ang six-year term ng President ay one-time lang.

text: The principle 'Public office is a public trust' is expressly stated in which Article of the 1987 Constitution?
optionA: Article II - Declaration of Principles and State Policies
optionD: Article XI - Accountability of Public Officers
explanation: Art. XI, Sec. 1 opens with 'Public office is a public trust' and requires public officers to be accountable to the people at all times.
hint: Look for the Article that deals with holding public officers answerable to the people.
whyA: Art. II has a related policy on honesty and integrity in the public service (Sec. 27), but the public-trust declaration is in Art. XI.
whyB: Art. III lists the rights of persons against the State, not the duties of public officers.
whyC: Art. IX creates the CSC, COMELEC and COA; it does not contain this declaration.
explanationTl: Nasa Art. XI, Sec. 1 ang 'Public office is a public trust.' Ibig sabihin, ang mga public officer ay dapat accountable sa taong-bayan sa lahat ng oras.
hintTl: Hanapin ang Article na tungkol sa pananagutan o accountability ng mga public officer.

text: Under the 1987 Constitution, the civil service covers government-owned or controlled corporations (GOCCs) that:
optionB: were organized under the general corporation law
optionC: are wholly owned by the government, whatever their charter
optionD: earn income from their own operations
explanation: Art. IX-B, Sec. 2(1) states that the civil service embraces all branches, subdivisions, instrumentalities and agencies of the Government, including GOCCs with original charters.
hint: The test is how the corporation was created, not how much the government owns.
whyB: GOCCs organized under the general corporation law do not have original charters, so they fall outside Art. IX-B, Sec. 2(1).
whyC: Ownership is not the test in the Constitution; the deciding factor is an original charter.
whyD: Whether a GOCC earns income has nothing to do with civil service coverage.
explanationTl: Sabi ng Art. IX-B, Sec. 2(1), sakop ng civil service ang lahat ng branches at agencies ng gobyerno, kasama ang mga GOCC na may original charter, ibig sabihin, nilikha ng sariling batas.
hintTl: Ang tanong dito ay kung paano nabuo ang corporation, hindi kung gaano kalaki ang share ng gobyerno.

text: Mario, a permanent clerk in a municipal treasurer's office, plans to campaign for a mayoral candidate after office hours. Under the 1987 Constitution, which statement is correct?
optionA: He may campaign as long as he does it outside office hours.
optionB: He may not engage, directly or indirectly, in any partisan political campaign.
optionC: He may campaign if he first files a leave of absence.
optionD: He may campaign only for candidates outside his own municipality.
explanation: Art. IX-B, Sec. 2(4) provides that no officer or employee in the civil service shall engage, directly or indirectly, in any electioneering or partisan political campaign. He keeps his right to vote.
hint: The ban covers both direct and indirect participation, with no exception for time or place.
whyA: The constitutional ban does not depend on office hours.
whyC: Going on leave does not lift the ban; he remains a civil service employee.
whyD: The ban covers any partisan political campaign, wherever the candidate runs.
explanationTl: Ayon sa Art. IX-B, Sec. 2(4), bawal sa kahit sinong civil service employee ang sumali, direct man o indirect, sa electioneering o partisan political campaign. Pwede pa rin siyang bumoto, pero bawal mangampanya.
hintTl: Sakop ng ban ang direct at indirect na pagsali, at walang exception kahit after office hours.

text: Ana ran for city councilor and lost. Under the 1987 Constitution, she may not be appointed to any office in the Government or in any GOCC or its subsidiaries within what period?
optionB: Until the term she ran for has ended
explanation: Art. IX-B, Sec. 6 provides that no candidate who has lost in any election shall, within one year after such election, be appointed to any office in the Government or any GOCC or in any of their subsidiaries.
hint: The ban is counted from the election date and is shorter than a full term of office.
whyA: Six months is too short; the Constitution sets a longer ban.
whyB: The ban is not tied to the term she ran for; it is a fixed period after the election.
whyC: Two years is longer than the period stated in Art. IX-B, Sec. 6.
explanationTl: Sa Art. IX-B, Sec. 6, ang natalong kandidato ay hindi pwedeng i-appoint sa kahit anong government office o GOCC sa loob ng one year after ng election. Para hindi gawing consolation prize ang pwesto sa gobyerno.
hintTl: Binibilang ito mula sa araw ng election, at mas maikli kaysa sa isang buong term.

text: In impeachment proceedings, what vote of all the Members of the House of Representatives is needed to affirm a favorable resolution with the Articles of Impeachment?
explanation: Art. XI, Sec. 3(3) states that a vote of at least one-third of all the Members of the House is necessary to affirm a favorable resolution with the Articles of Impeachment of the Committee, or to override its contrary resolution.
hint: The House only needs to send the case to trial, so its threshold is the lowest among the choices.
whyB: A majority is not the threshold; the Constitution sets a lower bar for the House.
whyC: Two-thirds of all the Senators is the vote needed to convict in the Senate (Art. XI, Sec. 3(6)), not to impeach in the House.
whyD: Three-fourths of all Members of Congress is the vote for proposing constitutional amendments (Art. XVII, Sec. 1), not for impeachment.
explanationTl: Sa Art. XI, Sec. 3(3), kailangan lang ng at least one-third ng lahat ng Members ng House para i-affirm ang Articles of Impeachment. Ang two-thirds ay para sa conviction sa Senate na.
hintTl: Ang House ay nagpapasa lang ng kaso papuntang trial, kaya pinakamababa ang kailangang boto dito.

text: Which of the following is NOT one of the norms of conduct listed in Section 4 of RA 6713?
explanation: RA 6713, Sec. 4 lists eight norms: commitment to public interest, professionalism, justness and sincerity, political neutrality, responsiveness to the public, nationalism and patriotism, commitment to democracy, and simple living. Loyalty to the appointing authority is not among them.
hint: The norms point public servants toward the public, not toward a particular person.
whyA: Professionalism is a norm under Sec. 4(b).
whyB: Political neutrality is a norm under Sec. 4(d).
whyD: Simple living is a norm under Sec. 4(h).
explanationTl: Walo ang norms of conduct sa RA 6713, Sec. 4: commitment to public interest, professionalism, justness and sincerity, political neutrality, responsiveness to the public, nationalism and patriotism, commitment to democracy, at simple living. Walang 'loyalty to the appointing authority' diyan.
hintTl: Ang norms ay naka-focus sa publiko, hindi sa isang tao o boss.

text: A municipal engineer and her family avoid flashy cars and lavish parties and live within their means. Which norm of conduct under RA 6713 does this reflect?
explanation: RA 6713, Sec. 4(h) requires public officials and employees and their families to lead modest lives appropriate to their positions and income and not to indulge in extravagant or ostentatious display of wealth.
hint: Focus on the lifestyle, not the work output.
whyA: Professionalism (Sec. 4(b)) is about performing duties with excellence and skill, not about lifestyle.
whyC: Responsiveness to the public (Sec. 4(e)) is about extending prompt and courteous service.
whyD: Nationalism and patriotism (Sec. 4(f)) is about loyalty to the Republic and the Filipino people.
explanationTl: Sa RA 6713, Sec. 4(h), ang public employees at ang family nila ay dapat mamuhay nang simple, ayon sa position at income nila, at hindi nagpapakita ng sobrang yaman o pagmamayabang.
hintTl: Tingnan mo ang lifestyle nila, hindi ang trabaho nila.

text: A resident sends a letter to a city office asking about her request. Under Section 5 of RA 6713, the office must respond to her letter within how many working days from receipt?
explanation: RA 6713, Sec. 5(a) requires public officials and employees to respond within fifteen (15) working days from receipt to letters and other communications sent by the public, and the reply must state the action taken.
hint: It is about three working weeks.
whyA: 3 working days is not the period set in RA 6713, Sec. 5(a).
whyB: 7 working days is shorter than the period set in RA 6713, Sec. 5(a).
whyC: 10 working days is shorter than the period set in RA 6713, Sec. 5(a).
explanationTl: Sa RA 6713, Sec. 5(a), dapat sagutin ng government office ang sulat ng publiko within 15 working days mula nang matanggap ito, at dapat nakasulat sa reply kung anong action ang ginawa.
hintTl: Mga tatlong working weeks ito.

text: Liza processes business permits at the municipal hall. An applicant whose permit is still pending gives her a new cellphone 'as thanks in advance.' She did not ask for it. Under RA 6713, which is correct?
optionA: She may not accept it, because it comes from a person whose transaction may be affected by her office.
optionB: She may keep it, because she did not solicit it.
optionC: She may keep it, provided she declares it in her SALN.
optionD: She may keep it once the permit has been released.
explanation: RA 6713, Sec. 7(d) prohibits public officials and employees from soliciting or accepting, directly or indirectly, any gift or anything of monetary value from any person in connection with any transaction which may be affected by the functions of their office.
hint: The law covers both asking for and receiving.
whyB: Sec. 7(d) prohibits accepting as well as soliciting, so not asking for it does not make it allowed.
whyC: Declaring a gift in the SALN does not cure a prohibited acceptance.
whyD: The gift is tied to her official transaction, so waiting until the permit is released does not make it allowed.
explanationTl: Sa RA 6713, Sec. 7(d), bawal mag-solicit o tumanggap ng regalo o anumang may monetary value mula sa taong may transaction na pwedeng maapektuhan ng trabaho mo. Kahit hindi niya hiningi, bawal pa ring tanggapin.
hintTl: Sakop ng batas hindi lang ang paghingi, kundi pati ang pagtanggap.

text: Carlo assumed office as an administrative aide on March 1. Under RA 6713, when must he file his first Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALN)?
optionA: On or before April 30 of the following year
optionB: Within 15 days after assumption of office
optionC: Within 30 days after assumption of office
optionD: Within 60 days after assumption of office
explanation: RA 6713, Sec. 8(A) requires the SALN to be filed within thirty (30) days after assumption of office, on or before April 30 of every year thereafter, and within thirty (30) days after separation from the service.
hint: The first filing is counted from the day he took office, not from a fixed calendar date.
whyA: April 30 is the deadline for the yearly filings after the first one, not for the first SALN.
whyB: 15 days is shorter than the period in Sec. 8(A).
whyD: 60 days is longer than the period in Sec. 8(A).
explanationTl: Sa RA 6713, Sec. 8(A), ang unang SALN ay dapat i-file within 30 days after mag-assume ng office. Pagkatapos noon, every year na on or before April 30, at within 30 days ulit pag umalis na sa service.
hintTl: Ang unang filing ay binibilang mula sa araw na nag-start siya, hindi sa fixed na date sa calendar.

text: Jun resigned from a government regulatory office. A private firm licensed by that office offers him a job as consultant. Under RA 6713, for how long after his resignation does the prohibition on such employment still apply to him?
explanation: RA 6713, Sec. 7(b) bars employment as consultant or officer in a private enterprise regulated, supervised or licensed by one's office, and states that these prohibitions continue to apply for one (1) year after resignation, retirement or separation from public office.
hint: The cooling-off period is shorter than a typical elective term.
whyA: Six months is shorter than the period stated in Sec. 7(b).
whyC: Two years is longer than the period stated in Sec. 7(b).
whyD: Five years is far longer than the period stated in Sec. 7(b).
explanationTl: Sa RA 6713, Sec. 7(b), bawal maging consultant o employee sa private company na nire-regulate o nili-license ng dati mong office, at tuloy pa rin ang bawal na ito for one year after mag-resign, mag-retire o ma-separate sa service.
hintTl: Ang 'cooling-off' period ay mas maikli kaysa sa isang elective term.

text: The Bill of Rights is found in which Article of the 1987 Constitution?
explanation: Article III of the 1987 Constitution is the Bill of Rights. Its Sec. 1 provides that no person shall be deprived of life, liberty or property without due process of law, nor be denied the equal protection of the laws.
hint: It comes right after the Declaration of Principles and State Policies.
whyB: Article II is the Declaration of Principles and State Policies.
whyC: Article VI is the Legislative Department.
whyD: Article XIII is Social Justice and Human Rights, which creates the CHR, but it is not the Bill of Rights.
explanationTl: Ang Bill of Rights ay nasa Article III. Sa Sec. 1 nito, walang tao na pwedeng alisan ng life, liberty o property nang walang due process, at lahat ay may equal protection of the laws.
hintTl: Sumunod ito agad sa Declaration of Principles and State Policies.

text: Human Rights Day is observed every December 10 because on that date in 1948 the United Nations General Assembly adopted the:
optionD: International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights
explanation: The UN General Assembly adopted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights on 10 December 1948 (Resolution 217 A (III)). Its Art. 1 declares that all human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights.
hint: It is a declaration, not a treaty or a charter.
whyA: The UN Charter was signed in 1945 and created the UN itself.
whyB: The Geneva Conventions on the laws of war were concluded in 1949 at a diplomatic conference.
whyD: The ICCPR was adopted later, in 1966.
explanationTl: Noong December 10, 1948, inadopt ng UN General Assembly ang Universal Declaration of Human Rights. Sa Art. 1 nito, lahat ng tao ay ipinanganak na malaya at pantay sa dignity at rights.
hintTl: Declaration ito, hindi treaty o charter.

text: During custodial investigation, a suspect tells the police he no longer wants a lawyer. Under Art. III, Sec. 12 of the 1987 Constitution, his waiver of the right to counsel is valid only if it is:
optionA: made orally and recorded on video
optionB: made in writing before the investigating officer
optionD: made in writing and in the presence of counsel
explanation: Art. III, Sec. 12(1) gives a person under investigation the right to remain silent and to have competent and independent counsel, and states that these rights cannot be waived except in writing and in the presence of counsel.
hint: Two conditions must both be present, and one of them is the very right being waived.
whyA: An oral waiver is not enough; the Constitution requires writing.
whyB: Writing alone is not enough; counsel must also be present.
whyC: Notarization is not the constitutional requirement; the presence of counsel is.
explanationTl: Sa Art. III, Sec. 12(1), ang suspect ay may right to remain silent at right to counsel. Pwede lang niyang i-waive ang mga ito kung in writing at may abogado na kasama mismo noong nag-waive siya.
hintTl: Dalawang kondisyon ang kailangan, at ang isa ay mismong 'yung right na wina-waive.

text: Under Article XIII, Section 18 of the 1987 Constitution, the Commission on Human Rights may investigate, on its own or on complaint by any party, all forms of human rights violations involving:
optionA: economic, social and cultural rights only
optionC: all crimes, with power to try and convict the offenders
optionD: administrative offenses of all civil servants
explanation: Art. XIII, Sec. 18(1) empowers the CHR to investigate, on its own or on complaint by any party, all forms of human rights violations involving civil and political rights.
hint: Think of rights like life, liberty, free speech and voting.
whyA: Sec. 18(1) refers to civil and political rights, not only economic, social and cultural rights.
whyC: The CHR investigates; it is not a court and cannot try or convict offenders.
whyD: Administrative discipline of civil servants belongs to other bodies such as the CSC and the Ombudsman, not the CHR.
explanationTl: Sa Art. XIII, Sec. 18(1), ang CHR ay pwedeng mag-investigate, kusa man o dahil may nag-complain, ng lahat ng human rights violations na may kinalaman sa civil and political rights.
hintTl: Isipin ang mga rights gaya ng right to life, liberty, free speech at pagboto.

text: Under RA 9003 (Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000), a Materials Recovery Facility (MRF) shall be established in every:
explanation: RA 9003, Sec. 32 provides that a Materials Recovery Facility shall be established in every barangay or cluster of barangays.
hint: Think of the smallest political unit, working alone or together with its neighbors.
whyA: The law places MRFs at a much more local level than the province.
whyB: Sec. 32 assigns MRFs to barangays or clusters of barangays, not only to cities or municipalities.
whyC: Households segregate waste at source, but the MRF is a barangay-level facility.
explanationTl: Sa RA 9003, Sec. 32, dapat may Materials Recovery Facility o MRF sa bawat barangay o cluster ng mga barangay.
hintTl: Isipin ang pinakamaliit na political unit, mag-isa man o kasama ng mga kalapit nito.

text: In Barangay Malinis, residents segregate their garbage at the source. Under RA 9003, who is responsible for collecting the non-recyclable materials and special wastes?
optionD: The Department of Environment and Natural Resources
explanation: RA 9003, Sec. 10 assigns the barangay to collect biodegradable, compostable and reusable wastes, while the collection of non-recyclable materials and special wastes is the responsibility of the municipality or city.
hint: The barangay handles the wastes that can be composted or reused; the harder wastes go one level up.
whyA: The barangay collects biodegradable, compostable and reusable wastes, not non-recyclables and special wastes.
whyB: Sec. 10 does not give this collection duty to the province.
whyD: The DENR sets standards and oversees; it does not do the actual collection.
explanationTl: Sa RA 9003, Sec. 10, ang barangay ang kumokolekta ng biodegradable, compostable at reusable na basura. Pero ang non-recyclable at special wastes, responsibility na ng municipality o city.
hintTl: Ang barangay ang bahala sa nabubulok at reusable; ang mas mahirap na basura, isang level pataas.

text: Republic Act No. 9275 is known as the:
optionC: Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000
optionD: Toxic Substances and Hazardous and Nuclear Wastes Control Act of 1990
explanation: RA 9275, Sec. 1 states that the Act shall be known as the Philippine Clean Water Act of 2004. It aims to protect the country's water bodies from pollution.
hint: Match the number to the most recent year among the choices.
whyB: The Philippine Clean Air Act of 1999 is RA 8749.
whyC: The Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000 is RA 9003.
whyD: The Toxic Substances and Hazardous and Nuclear Wastes Control Act of 1990 is RA 6969.
explanationTl: Sa RA 9275, Sec. 1, ang batas na ito ay tinatawag na Philippine Clean Water Act of 2004. Layunin nitong protektahan ang mga katubigan ng bansa laban sa polusyon.
hintTl: Itugma ang number sa pinakabagong taon sa mga choices.
